ai.description: *Microhyla kodial* is a tiny frog (18–20 mm) with a brownish-grey dorsum and a distinct dark, diamond-shaped dorsal pattern. It features a pointed snout and lacks webbing on its toes.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Microhyla kodial* is best distinguished by the absence of a dark dorsal marking, appearing plain brownish-grey compared to the patterned backs of other Indian *Microhyla*.
ai.habitat: *Microhyla kodial* inhabits urban and semi-urban landscapes in coastal Karnataka, specifically breeding in temporary rain-filled ditches and puddles near human settlements.
ai.behavior: *Microhyla kodial* is primarily nocturnal, emerging during the monsoon to forage for small insects and invertebrates among leaf litter and damp soil.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Microhyla kodial* breeds during the monsoon, laying eggs in small, temporary rain-filled pools. Females deposit clutches of approximately 200–300 eggs in the water.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Microhyla kodial* is endemic to a single urban locality in Mangaluru, Karnataka, situated in the coastal lowlands of the Western Ghats.
ai.callDescription: The *Microhyla kodial* produces a high-pitched, insect-like buzzing call with a rapid, rhythmic pulse, typically heard from temporary rain pools in urban Mangaluru habitats.
